source.title: Understanding Activation Patterns in Artificial Neural Networks by Exploring Stochastic Processes
source.authors: S. Lehmler; Muhammad Saif-ur-Rehman; T. Glasmachers; Ioannis Iossifidis

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether networks trained on natural labels generalize while versions trained on shuffled labels memorize, using classification accuracy and activation statistics rather than reproducing Zhang et al.'s experiments.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports train and validation accuracy for natural-label training and three shuffled-label memorization settings. The extracted accuracy rows cover V1. The paper also measures firing-rate and Fano-factor statistics, but those results do not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness named in V7 or the test-error behavior named in V2.
record.test_reason: Table 1 tests V1's coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization in additional architectures and datasets. It also tests V3 through matched-width CNN versus MLP validation accuracies on MNIST and FashionMNIST. Deliberately randomized labels directly test the capacity named in V1. The activation-statistic analyses do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors propose stochastic modeling of thresholded activations and find promising distinctions between natural-label generalization and randomized-label memorization. Lower mean firing rates characterize memorization most clearly when the observed layer must perform it; width and earlier trainable layers weaken the distinction. They report similar activation distributions on training and test inputs, but acknowledge imperfect Poisson fit and limited extrapolation from forced memorization.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with learning rate 0.1, no momentum and batch size 256; tests natural and shuffled labels on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 with selected MLP/CNN/DenseNet architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, architecture, hidden-layer width, and which layers are allowed to train during shuffled-label memorization affect fit or activation-statistic comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean firing rates and Fano statistics distinguish many shuffled-label memorizing networks from natural-label generalizing networks, with sensitivity to observed-layer width and which layers can train.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-hidden-layer activation statistics can indicate randomized-label memorization under specified architecture and training conditions; these are distinct from magnitude-aware sharpness.

record.problems: Memorization was forced using randomized labels; several shuffled-label settings did not reach high training accuracy. The paper studies selected image-classification datasets and models, observes only the last hidden layer for activation analyses, and reports validation rather than a separately named test split in Table 1. The flattened table makes some CNN and DenseNet method-to-value mappings difficult to assign.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 has separate training/validation pairs for additional shuffled-label conditions. To stay within 60 rows, the extraction prioritizes natural-label performance and two shuffled-label methods; the remaining MemRetrainAll accuracy results are not extracted. Table 1's flattened layout also prevents reliable assignment of some displayed values to CNN and DenseNet settings.

untested.parts: The original Inception/AlexNet and ImageNet experiments are not reproduced. The memorization conditions change initialization or freeze layers; they do not all preserve the natural-label training recipe. No explicit regularization is described, but its absence is not comprehensively documented.

No width sweep establishes zero natural-label training error followed by continued test-error improvement under training to convergence. MLP natural-label training accuracy remains below 100% at every width.
Local connectivity is not isolated from weight sharing and added architecture. Sparse fully connected learning, convolution-derived initialization, CIFAR-100 and SVHN comparisons are not tested.
No held-out optimizer comparison is reported.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measure or comparison with norm and margin measures is reported.
No removal and retraining experiment based on example memorization scores is reported.

missing.what: CNN FashionMNIST MemRetrainLast rows are missing: widths 64, 128, 256 and 512 respectively have train/validation accuracies 61.55/10.33, 91.38/9.82, 99.67/10.23 and 99.99/9.52 percent. These distinguish incomplete fitting at narrower widths from near-perfect fitting at larger widths.
missing.locator: Table 1, MemRetrainLast column, CNN FashionMNIST entries

record.verdict_notes: The flattened Table 1 is recoverable by following its ordered dataset pairs; most extracted shuffled-label values were assigned to the wrong configurations. Validation accuracies use the reported 10% validation split and should not be relabeled as official test-set accuracies. R14 requires version-specific interpretation: reversed for V3, observed for V1's natural-label component. MemRetrainAll results are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as missing or used for additional verdicts. This study is not an original source of the tested versions.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses MLPs, CNNs and a pretrained DenseNet121 feature extractor on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10; it does not test the small Inception, AlexNet, or ImageNet settings named in the version.
